messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build a **RESTful GET request** against the Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) API that will return the *Speed* information for a specific interface. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Query Parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | | **Full URL** | `https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed` | | **Authentication** | Basic Auth (username/password) or Bearer token – whichever is configured on your ND instance. | | **Headers** | `Accept: application/json`
`Content-Type: application/json`
`Authorization: Basic ` (or `Bearer `) | --- ## 1. Build the URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo ``` Add the query string: ```text ?fabricName=Network1 &nodeId=12 &podId=10 &interfaceType=ethernet &infoType=Speed ``` Result: ``` https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` > **Tip:** URL‑encode the values if they contain special characters (not needed here). --- ## 2. Authentication ### Basic Auth ```bash curl -u : \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` ### Bearer Token ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` --- ## 3. Example with `curl` ```bash curl -k \ -u admin:admin123 \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` > `-k` skips certificate verification (use only in test environments). --- ## 4. Example with Python (`requests`) ```python import requests from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } response = requests.get( url, params=params, auth=HTTPBasicAuth("admin", "admin123"), headers={"Accept": "application/json"}, verify=False # skip cert check for demo; remove in prod ) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 5. Using the Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI 1. Log into the ND web UI. 2. Navigate to **Developer → API Explorer** (or **Developer → REST API**). 3. Select the **GET** method and paste the full URL. 4. Add the required headers (`Accept`, `Content-Type`, `Authorization`). 5. Click **Send** – the response pane will show the JSON payload. --- ## 6. Using the provided tool (Python function) If you want to invoke the request programmatically via the helper function: ```json { "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", "params": { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } } ``` ```python result = functions.requests_get({ "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", "params": { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } }) print(result) ``` --- ### What you’ll receive The ND API will return a JSON object similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speed": "1000Mbps" } ``` (Actual field names may vary; consult the ND API docs for the exact schema.) --- ### Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Verify credentials or token; ensure the account has API access. | | **404 Not Found** | Double‑check the endpoint path; ensure the API version matches your ND release. | | **400 Bad Request** | Ensure all required query parameters are present and correctly typed. | | **SSL errors** | Use `-k` in curl or `verify=False` in Python for self‑signed certs; otherwise install the proper CA. | --- That’s it! With the URL, query parameters, headers, and authentication in place, you can hit the ND API to retrieve the interface speed information. Happy querying!
